findings.evidence: "the head glyphs schematic: the canonical model has 64 query and 64 KV heads per layer (Ch. 4, Table 4-2), so the four drawn heads stand for the enumeration, not the model's head count. The token labels mark sequence positions, not the sampled-versus-input distinction"
findings.issue: The caption first says the four drawn heads 'stand for the enumeration, not the model's head count' (i.e. a schematic abbreviation), then immediately says 'the token labels mark sequence positions, not the sampled-versus-input distinction, so the one-step write offset described above is stated in this caption rather than drawn.' The caption simultaneously tells the reader the drawing is schematic (heads, tokens) AND that it accurately represents sequence positions — two contradictory readings of what the figure encodes. A reader cannot tell whether token₁/token₂/token₃ labels are a faithful representation of sequence positions or another schematic abbreviation.
findings.fix_instruction: Make the schematic-scope statement uniform across the caption: either state that token labels are also schematic (like the head glyphs), or rephrase to distinguish explicitly which elements are faithful (positions) and which are abbreviated (head count).

findings.evidence: "(All figures trace to the canonical scenario (Ch. 4, Table 4-2); none are measurement claims.)"
findings.issue: The table header calls every row '(worked example, not reference)' and says 'none are measurement claims,' but the first two rows ('input tokens / request ~9,200' and 'output tokens / request ~300') carry no [DERIVED] label — they are the [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION] inputs. The remaining rows are [DERIVED]. Calling an assumed input a 'worked example' conflates input with computation: an assumption is the scenario setup, not a worked result. The header's blanket classification hides the Assumption/Derived split that the book's own evidence discipline (Preface, §2-axis note) requires.
findings.fix_instruction: Either add the [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION] labels to the first two rows and [canonical scenario][DERIVED] to the computed rows (matching Table 1-1's derivation column pattern), or change the header to '(assumed inputs and derived results of the canonical scenario)' rather than '(worked example, not reference)'.

findings.page: PDF p. 27 (book p. 4); cross-refs at PDF p. 21 (Preface) and PDF pp. 62, 74 (Ch. 3)
findings.chapter: Ch. 1 — It All Starts With the First Token (cross-reference form)
findings.evidence: Ch. 1 §1.1.2, PDF p. 27: "... DeepSeek-V4 technical report, arXiv 2606.19348, and model card HF deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro — all accessed 2026-08-30, the book's evidence cutoff; A.10" and again "model card HF Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, accessed 2026-08-30; A.10".  Preface, PDF p. 21: "Appendix A, A.6 carries a boxed 2026-09-27 capability probe ..." and "a superseding re-verification of the DeepSeek model-service status (Appendix A, A.3)".  Ch. 3, PDF p. 74: "is in Appendix A §9A, 'Noise-stage expert selection (Wan2.2 A14B)'"; PDF p. 62: "carried in Appendix A §9A (alternative inference in detail)".  Stated convention, Preface PDF p. 23: "Appendix A numbers its own sections with a letter suffix, so Appendix A § 9A means Appendix A, the section labelled 9A; the appendix's figures carry A.N."
findings.issue: Three incompatible forms are used for the same class of reference: "A.10" and "A.6"/"A.3" (letter-dot-digit, used for appendix sections) and "§9A" (digit-then-letter, the form the Preface declares normative). "A.10" additionally collides with the appendix's figure numbering scheme (A.N per the Preface and the List of Figures, A.1–A.5), so a reader cannot tell whether it points at section 10A, figure A.10, or nothing — and no A.10 figure exists in the List of Figures.
findings.fix_instruction: Normalise every appendix cross-reference to the declared convention ("Appendix A §10A", "Appendix A §6A", "Appendix A §3A", "Appendix A §9A"), reserving "A.N" exclusively for figures and tables. Sweep the whole book for the "A.N"-as-section form (it currently appears at least three times) and rewrite them.

findings.chapter: Ch. 1 — It All Starts With the First Token
findings.evidence: §1.1.2: "Current-gen models commonly ship windows ranging from roughly 8K tokens in older or small-tier deployments up to a million-plus tokens at the frontier, varying by model and vendor — for example, the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next card states a native 262K-token window with YaRN extension to 1M, and the GLM-5.3-Flash and DeepSeek-V4 cards state 1M [1P][FACT] ... ; the low end of that range is the older/edge tier rather than a published figure for a current frontier model [1P][HYPOTHESIS]."
findings.issue: The [1P] provenance is applied to a statement that is the book's own market characterization ("the low end of that range is the older/edge tier rather than a published figure for a current frontier model"), not to anything a vendor published — the same paragraph's card-derived statements are correctly tagged [1P][FACT]. The book's own Axis-1 definition is "[1P] — first-party: the model vendor's own spec", and the Preface warns against provenance/status mismatch.
findings.fix_instruction: Re-tag this clause so the provenance matches its origin — e.g. [2°][HYPOTHESIS] (second-hand survey of vendor line-ups) or [canonical scenario][HYPOTHESIS] — or restate it as an explicitly author-chosen framing without an [1P] provenance, keeping [1P][FACT] only for the card-stated windows.
